earlier_scan.source_named: Holzknecht, Susanne. 1989. The Markham languages of Papua New Guinea. Pacific Linguistics C-115 (doctype: phonology; covers Sarasira/Adzera cluster). No open scan found.

sources.citation: Holzknecht, Susanne. 1986. A morphology and grammar of Adzera (Amari dialect). Papers in New Guinea Linguistics 24 (PL A-70), 77-166. Sec. 2.5 Stress, p. 94. [related language ADZERA adze1240, read for context only]
sources.note: 'Stress in Amari is not phonemic. In general, the first syllable of a two-syllable word is stressed, and in words of more than two syllables, the first syllable is stressed, and then every alternate syllable is stressed.' This describes Adzera (Amari dialect), a different language of the Upper Markham group (Adzera subgroup, not the Mountain subgroup Sarasira belongs to); NOT used as a Sarasira statement.
sources.venue: Papers in New Guinea Linguistics 24 (PL A-70)

sources.citation: OLAC. Resources in and about the Sarasira language (zsa), as of 2025-07-08.
sources.note: Lists 11 PARADISEC audio items from Holzknecht's 1985 fieldwork (SH2-ANUA520_4020, _5001-_5008, _5011: Sarasira 1-6, Songs 1-2, a story) plus Glottolog; no written language description of any kind.

sources.citation: ISO 639-3 Registration Authority. 2007. Change Request 2007-186 (D. Howard, SIL PNG; supported by S. Holzknecht): split azr into adz Adzera, zsa Sarasira, zsu Sukurum; adopted 2008-01-14.
sources.note: Identity only: Sarasira and Sukurum 'more closely related to the Mari and Wampur languages.. Mountain subgroup of Upper Markham'; sources cited are Holzknecht 1989 and Ross 1988. No phonology.

sources.citation: Holzknecht, Susanne. 1989. The Markham languages of Papua New Guinea. Pacific Linguistics C-115. Canberra: ANU. viii+228 pp. DOI 10.15144/PL-C115 (Glottolog ref 158598). Sec. 4.2.5 Sarasira, p. 53.
sources.harvard_location: Widener Library (offsite storage), call number PL5026 .H64 1989
sources.note: Sec. 4.2.5 (p. 53) is a phoneme table (Table 4.6) plus four allophony notes (word-final /h/; back-velar /g,k/; r~d~l free; /h/ rare). Nothing on stress, accent, tone, syllable structure or prosody. Ch. 4 intro (p. 50): 'brief phonological statement of each of the Markham languages. Full phonological statements are to be published at a later date.' The word 'stress' occurs in the book only in an Adzera dialect-perception remark, a Duwet note on unstressed vowel sequences, and a Watut historical remark; none concerns Sarasira.

tone.quote: None of the Markham languages, except Labu, has more than five vowels, and they are presented in the phonological sketches. Labu, however, does have a seven-vowel system, probably borrowed through intensive contact with Bukawa speakers. Labu also has phonemic tone on its vowels, and is the only Markham language with this feature. Again, this has almost certainly been borrowed from Bukawa.

sources.citation: Holzknecht, Susanne C. 1988. The Markham languages of Papua New Guinea: a history of the Austronesian languages of the Markham and Ramu Valleys. PhD thesis, ANU. hdl 1885/133945.
sources.note: Same content as the 1989 book; stress/accent hits identical (Adzera perception remark, Duwet note, Watut 'stress rules'); nothing for Sarasira.

sources.citation: Ross, Malcolm. 1988. Proto Oceanic and the Austronesian languages of western Melanesia. Pacific Linguistics C-98. Canberra: ANU. DOI 10.15144/PL-C98 (Glottolog ref 98107).

sources.harvard_location: Widener Library (offsite storage), call number PL6201 .R67 1988
sources.note: Sarasira/Sirasira appears only in the Markham classification list, sound-correspondence tables and cognate sets; the book's stress remarks concern Ali/Kairiru and PMK *ai reduction, not Sarasira. No synchronic stress statement.

sources.citation: Smith, Geoffrey P. 1988. Morobe counting systems. In Papers in New Guinea Linguistics 26 (Pacific Linguistics A-76), 1-132. DOI 10.15144/PL-A76.1 (Glottolog ref 8921).
sources.note: Sec. 23 'Sirasira' (p. ~70): six numerals from Som and Sirasira informants, unmarked for stress; conventions (p. 54) only define a symbol for an 'unaccented neutral vowel'. No stress statement.
sources.venue: Papers in New Guinea Linguistics 26 (Pacific Linguistics A-76)

sources.citation: Hooley, Bruce A. 1971. Austronesian languages of the Morobe District, Papua New Guinea. Oceanic Linguistics 10(2): 79-151.
sources.note: Only other Glottolog-listed source with Sarasira ('Sirasira') primary data (wordlists for lexicostatistics); may carry a note on transcription conventions, though unlikely to state a stress rule.
